title: Trace Garden — Weekly reflections and action log (2026-11-20)
notes:
Week snapshot (Nov 15–21)

Purpose: short, messy capture of what we actually talked about in standups + the small experiments we tried so we don't lose context. Not a finished runbook.

Attendees (recurring): Maya, Ravi, Elena, Diego, Jun. Ad-hoc: Sasha (platform), Priya (billing).

Highlights
- Trace sampling experiment #7 (prefix-aware dynamic sampling) went live to 10% of production on Tue; initial cost delta: -3.8% trace ingest cost on the sampled shard, end-to-end retention unchanged for high-latency flows.
- New dashboard tile for per-route KV-cache hit rate shipped to staging and validated with canary traffic. Dashboard id: kv-hit-v2 (temp).
- Cost telemetry alarm (billing-telemetry-spike) tuned to ignore scheduled backfills after noisy week. Reduced false positives from 6/day -> 1/week.

Standup snippets (one-liners, prioritized)
- Maya: debugged trace-loss for multi-hop calls — root cause was the nginx proxy stripping x-request-id on some 504s; patch rolled to canary.
- Ravi: completed prometheus -> clickhouse export adapter for span metrics; seeing 30% lower write amplification. TODO: add back-pressure knob.
- Elena: trimmed dashboard queries, replaced several nested OR filters with explicit union queries; reduced average panel load time from 1.6s -> 0.8s.
- Diego: validated cold-start sampling config for ephemeral jobs; we should avoid < 100ms delay in sampling path.
- Jun: rerun of trace-replay with 25k reqs; KV cache hit increases correlated with batching improvements.

Decisions made
- Keep prefix-aware dynamic sampling in 10% canary for two more weeks. If cost delta stays >= -3% with no customer regressions, schedule gradual ramp. Owner: Maya.
- Rollback plan: if we see >1% increase in tail p99 latency attributable to sampling, immediately revert sampling keys for the impacted route. Owner: Ravi.
- Dashboard retention: keep 14-day high-cardinality traces, 90-day aggregated metrics. Elena to add TTL note to dashboard descriptions.

Open questions / Risks (not resolved)
- Are we undercounting trace volume due to lost spans at the proxy layer? Need concrete measurement approach (synthetic traffic + header checksum).
- Interaction between sampling and rerankers: does sampling bias evaluation metrics for rerank experiments? Action: Jun to model expected bias.

Experiment log (short)
- Prefix-aware dynamic sampling v0.7
  - Variant: sample by route prefix + short-term frequency factor (LRU count).
  - Observation: reduces backend write QPS by ~7% on canary shard; pipeline CPU down ~5%.
  - Unexpected: a few low-volume enterprise routes lost sufficient spans to affect alerting thresholds. Mitigation: whitelisting for known low-volume but high-importance routes.

- KV-cache hit dashboard tweak
  - Query: changed GROUP BY window to 1m -> 5m for summary panels; reduces series cardinality but still useful for quick triage.
  - Next: add per-customer drill link to trace search for top 10 misses.

Action items (concrete, owner, due)
- Maya: instrument proxy synthetic header checksum test, run 24h and report mismatch rate. Due: 2026-11-24.
- Ravi: add back-pressure configuration toggle to exporter and stage tests. Due: 2026-11-26.
- Elena: annotate three heavy dashboards with retention/TTL and query rationale. Due: 2026-11-25.
- Diego: produce a short doc on cold-start sampling constraints (100ms threshold) and add to runbook. Due: 2026-11-28.
- Jun: simulate reranker evaluation with sampled traces and produce bias estimate. Due: 2026-11-29.

Notes to self / fragmented brainstorm
- Could we make the sampling decision graph-based instead of prefix-only? e.g., sample strongly for traces that touch service A+B+C combos. Might capture multi-hop tail better. Complexity tradeoff: cardinality explosion vs better signal.
- Consider lightweight per-route whitelists stored in config service with hot reload — avoids frequent deploys for urgent whitelists.
- Billing signal: explore embedding a coarse token-count estimate into spans so billing team can reconcile trace-based cost signals with token-based billing.

Meeting follow-ups scheduled
- Fri 2026-11-26: hot-seat review for sampling canary (15m) — owners: Maya + Ravi.
- Mon 2026-11-29: dashboard cost debt grooming (30m) — owner: Elena.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Linear: RED-4783 (sampling canary), OBS-502 (dashboard query perf)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/221 (exporter adapter)
- Confluence: OBSV telemetry roadmap (bookmark)

End of week notes — keep as a living doc. If anything here needs to exist in a polished runbook, move to confluence and link.
